newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian job ads data briefly dents bond rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian job ads data briefly dents bond rally.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were close to the day's lows ahead of the lunchtime recess, although a sharp jump in the ANZ's job advertisement briefly knocked the rally off course.
*Full labour force report due on Thursday.
Australian bond yields were close to the day's lows ahead of the lunchtime recess, although a sharp jump in the ANZ's job advertisement series briefly knocked the U.S.-led rally off course.
April job ads rose a record monthly 16.7 percent, although this was partly due to the earlier timing of Easter. But even allowing for this, ANZ said ads would have risen 5.0 percent.

"We should expect to see some improvement in the official employment statistics over the next few months, in contrast to the outright declines in employment reported for February and March," said ANZ's chief economist Saul Eslake.

Australia releases its full labour force report on Thursday, data which economists expect to show a rebound in employment, although insufficient to make an impression on the stubbornly high unemployment rate.

Further strength in U.S. Treasuries on Friday after a balanced budget accord was achieved triggered off the local rally, which saw key resistance overcome on the local 10-year bond futures contract as the market played catch-up after underperforming in the past few sessions.
The market has been under pressure since stronger than expected wages data last week killed vague hopes of a rate cut.

The Reserve Bank holds its monthly board meeting, although economists do not expect any change in policy to follow the meeting, and a majority now see the next move as a tightening, likely in the first quarter of next year.

There is little in the way of key data out of the U.S. this week, although U.S. Treasuries face the quarterly refunding auctions with US$17.0 billion of three-year notes on offer on Tuesday and US$12.0 nillion of 10-year notes on Wednesday.

The local market outperformed against the dollar bloc, apart from the short end of the Canadian yield curve. The Canadian out-paced the U.S. on Friday amid further strength in the Canadian dollar on waning fears of a U.S. policy tightening.
The 10-year bond contract is now looking to test April's 92.250 high after a strong test of major resistance at 92.210/92.230 during the morning session.
